pr_title: fix: further improvements to effect scheduling and flushing
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/issues/10946

This a follow up to [10949](https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/pull/10949). Now we have true topological ordering of effects, it makes sense to try and improve certain parts of the processing of the nested effects.

Whilst looking into the bug referenced above, I noticed that we traverse into inert/destroyed effect trees, which is just pointless. I also noticed that maybe after the refactors in this PR, maybe we could just invoke render effects directly. Everything passes but one e2e test to do with custom elements. So maybe this is promising!

I also noticed that flushing of local render effects wasn't correctly setting the counter back to zero like we do in other places – which is another reported issue when using legacy effects with `beforeUpdate`, as that triggers this code path. I added a test to capture that not failing.

issue_context.title: Svelte 5: ERR_SVELTE_TOO_MANY_UPDATES
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

This is a bug I've experienced since I started using Svelte 5 (so like from next.30 and up).

I have a todo list with todos.

I can make a new todo just fine when there is less than 30 todos in the todo list.

When there is more than 30-something todos, then I get the "ERR_SVELTE_TOO_MANY_UPDATES".

_I think it is very clear that there isn't a infinite loop here, just the 100 flush_count limit being reached_

The error does not come from any of my $effect (i've logged every single one, none of them are experiencing an infinite loop), so I assume it must come from the template somehow.

I haven't tested my $dervied (can it come from there? It clearly says "execute_effect" in the stack trace).

I am using a svelte 4 UI library (https://konstaui.com/), maybe the mixing is causing some problems (?)

### Reproduction
